newsitem.title: UK: London robusta coffee futures hit 16-month high.
newsitem.headline: London robusta coffee futures hit 16-month high.

text.p: London robusta coffee futures scaled a 16-month high of $2,200 a tonne basis July on Wednesday on frenzied buying inspired by surging New York futures for the arabica type of beans.

By 1427 GMT, the July contract was up $98 on the day at $2,200. New York's July contract hit a new 20-year-high of $2.91 on Wednesday on heightened fears of cold weather in top grower Brazil later this week.
The spectacular rally since early January has doubled the value of arabicas, triggering retail price increases in Europe and the United States.
Stocks in producer and consuming countries are at 20-year lows and there are concerns that a frost in Brazil could damage the crop there.
Already there has been a shortfall in coffee from Colombia, the largest producer after Brazil.

"...This makes the market extremely prone to weather scares in Brazil, even at this early stage of the season," broker GNI said in a commentary. The last severe frosts in 1994, one in June and another in July, damaged many coffee trees and sent world prices sky-rocketing. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
